security_semantics_audit.area: credentials, issuance epochs, handoff, and sole-owner rotation
security_semantics_audit.basis: The selected R10/R11 and corrected DC09 boundary preserves historical issuance epoch, requires a second active owner credential before rotation, closes active/revoked state, binds one-time locator delivery, forbids re-reveal, and distinguishes ordinary delivery failure from GKOS_P6_SECRET_EXPOSURE. The registry includes the seven authentication non-enumeration leaves, issue/rotate results, prior-credential reconnect, zero-grace, lost-handoff, and sole-owner conflict leaves. This does not overcome the registry integrity and ambiguity findings.

The selected rules forbid raw paths and bind canonical relative names, physical identity, content, protection, ownership, regular-file and no-link evidence. Unsafe attacker objects are not deleted. No product qualification is implied.

Q2 and corrected R07/DC11 unambiguously invalidate reference-bound cursors after restart, project CURSOR_STALE to GKOS_P6_REQUEST_STALE_AUTHORITY, evaluate restart invalidation before reference lookup, disclose no prior existence, and require rediscovery. Durable resolver state and cross-restart continuation are forbidden.

Pre-adapter mapping operations return GKOS_P6_PLATFORM_UNAVAILABLE without mapping-existence disclosure. Authenticated subject evidence, collision guard, digest domain/preimage/equality, adapter binding, and adapter-enabled subject-digest collision qualification are deferred together. GKOS_P6_IDENTITY_COLLISION remains among exactly 53 codes, and ordinary binding conflict remains GKOS_P6_MAPPING_CONFLICT.

The rule preserves one entropy use, zero mutation, no retry, no overwrite, and content-free evidence, and the registry enumerates non-mapping identifier classes. COLLISION-ID-IDEMPOTENCY-001 nevertheless permits either GKOS_P6_IDENTITY_COLLISION or an unspecified idempotency-conflict projection for one canonical fixture ID.

findings.title: The frozen registry source ledger binds superseded correction-map and owner-resolution bytes
evidence: The registry source_trace binds the correction map as d6f2a803452206001fc10d65c64e79996fa91c6604ddb7658cb67aefd65d01ac / 22841 bytes, while the exact concurrence input is 87da54d22f72e27625144143e15dcc6a38264b856af51bdaf5d26055a92c2a29 / 21418 bytes.

The registry source_trace binds owner resolution V2 as de6a4b034bec87e7819d674abbdf4bd2ebd73529d0caf7bec14e62431712bc14 / 6548 bytes, while the exact concurrence input is 95b8bc0b7fdb646a8a40f244526df5d8ac6a34384124a40c338366d843f62d84 / 8395 bytes.
Owner resolution V2 requires every concurrence to bind the same exact correction-map, resolution, and registry bytes and says any byte drift or fixture-registry disagreement restarts C1 through C3.
findings.impact: The registry is cryptographically intact as its own artifact but is not evidence derived from, or mutually bound to, the current exact correction coordinate. Accepting it would waive an explicit exact-byte security gate.
findings.required_disposition: Remain stopped and return to the Product Owner. A replacement registry/correction-map/resolution coordinate must be produced and ratified without editing these immutable reviewed bytes; all dependent concurrences must restart against the new exact hashes.

findings.title: Several frozen canonical fixture IDs allow alternative or unnamed security outcomes
evidence: COLLISION-ID-IDEMPOTENCY-001 permits GKOS_P6_IDENTITY_COLLISION or an existing exact idempotency-conflict projection.

GLOBAL-EVENT-COORDINATES-001 permits GKOS_P6_AUTHORITY_CORRUPT or transaction rollback; GLOBAL-EVENT-DUPLICATE-ID-001 and GLOBAL-EVENT-KIND-TABLE-001 combine insertion and startup outcomes; GLOBAL-EVENT-DUPLICATE-SEQUENCE-001 names only a closed conflict/corruption outcome.
POLICY-INDETERMINATE-001 permits a policy-unavailable or denied projection and POLICY-TIMEOUT-001 permits a timeout or policy projection.
REFERENCE-CROSS-SESSION-001 and REFERENCE-PROCESS-RESTART-001 name stale or invalid-reference responses, while RESTORE-ABORT-UNSAFE-001 permits ABORTED or blocked.

The registry declares one ID equals one executable leaf and freezes each expected semantic, while the owner resolution forbids adding, splitting, merging, or reinterpreting fixtures without a new owner decision.
findings.impact: A successor-F1 author would have to choose, split, or condition these outcomes, thereby contributing security semantics and potentially changing the ratified count/hash. Byte-identical non-enumeration and exact error projection cannot be proven from a fixture that admits more than one result.
findings.required_disposition: The Product Owner must ratify the complete required_correction_inventory in this artifact or an equivalently exact replacement: exact split IDs, exact per-leaf initial state and schedule, exact existing code or state result, and recomputed counts and hashes. Fresh C1 through C3 concurrences are then required.
